validation-loss-stuck-high-parameter-ext.error_identification: Validation MSE remains high and is dominated by alive-count dimensions. Multiple calibrated parameters hit bounds (LOS means collapse to 1; ICU routing collapses to 0/1), indicating the optimizer is compensating for structural mismatch rather than finding stable, generalizable dynamics.
validation-loss-stuck-high-parameter-ext.root_cause_analysis: Current dynamics can only change alive counts through LOS-based discharge with a (mostly) stationary arrival model and fixed bed assignment. The extreme fitted parameters suggest the model cannot match disease-specific alive trajectories with just per-disease Poisson arrivals + a mean-scaled empirical LOS sampler, so it drives LOS to minimum and forces bed routing extremes to indirectly shape occupancy/alive counts. Likely missing: disease-specific LOS shape (not just mean scaling) and/or stronger nonstationarity/trajectory heterogeneity in arrivals than the global day-profile provides.
validation-loss-stuck-high-parameter-ext.correct_approach: Within existing 12-parameter interface, reduce the need for extreme compensation by: (1) replacing mean-scaling of empirical LOS with a discrete reweighting scheme that preserves integer support but shifts mass smoothly (e.g., exponential tilting over observed LOS values) per (disease, bed) using the los_mean parameter as a control; this allows shape adaptation without collapsing to LOS=1. Implement in HospitalFlowModel._sample_los by computing tilted probabilities over info['values'] based on a temperature/tilt derived from target_mean vs empirical mean, then sample from tilted probs. (2) Make arrival nonstationarity disease-specific but also allow trajectory-level randomness: in HospitalFlowModel.rollout, draw a per-trajectory multiplicative random effect for each disease (mean 1, moderate variance) applied to arrival_lambda_for_day; this improves cross-trajectory generalization without changing theta dimensionality. Keep the effect deterministic given seed and trajectory_id to avoid training/val leakage.
validation-loss-stuck-high-parameter-ext.key_insight: When calibrated parameters consistently hit bounds, treat it as evidence the simulator’s latent degrees of freedom (distribution shapes and heterogeneity) are insufficient; add shape/heterogeneity mechanisms before further tuning.

arrival-profile-derived-from-train-may-o.error_identification: Day-varying arrival modulation learned from the entire training set does not improve validation and can encode split-specific temporal structure that does not transfer, while also being non-parameterized (not part of θ) and therefore not properly inferred by SBI.
arrival-profile-derived-from-train-may-o.root_cause_analysis: HospitalFlowModel.ingest_training_statistics learns _arrival_profile_scale directly from train data and then uses it during both calibration and evaluation. This adds a strong, fixed, non-θ component to the simulator. Because SBI only infers θ, any data-derived profile acts like an unmodeled, hard-coded prior that may fit training idiosyncrasies and reduce identifiability/generalization.
arrival-profile-derived-from-train-may-o.correct_approach: Gate or simplify the arrival profile so it cannot overfit: (1) Change ingest_training_statistics to compute a single smooth seasonality curve shared across diseases (or a very low-rank representation) rather than a full length-T per-disease profile; keep it normalized to mean 1. (2) Add an on/off toggle (default off) for using _arrival_profile_scale during calibration/evaluation, and evaluate whether val_loss improves with it disabled. (3) If kept on, compute the profile from train_states[0] only (matching x_o) to avoid injecting information from other training trajectories into the simulator used for inference.
arrival-profile-derived-from-train-may-o.key_insight: Avoid injecting non-θ, data-derived dynamics into the simulator unless they are part of the inference target; otherwise SBI optimizes against a moving/hidden mechanism and generalization suffers.

los-empirical-scaling-rounding-causes-di.error_identification: Even with empirical LOS values, scaling individual draws by target_mean/emp_mean and rounding can create unrealistic LOS mass at 1 (or other small integers), changing discharge hazards and producing persistent occupancy/alive errors.
los-empirical-scaling-rounding-causes-di.root_cause_analysis: In HospitalFlowModel._sample_los, LOS is sampled from empirical values then multiplied by a scale and rounded. This transforms the distribution in a non-smooth, value-dependent way and can concentrate probability mass at small integers after rounding/clipping, especially when target_mean is driven low by calibration.
los-empirical-scaling-rounding-causes-di.correct_approach: Replace per-sample scaling with probability reweighting over the original empirical support: keep info['values'] unchanged, compute new probabilities proportional to probs * f(values; tilt) where tilt is chosen to match (approximately) the desired mean implied by los_mean, then sample directly from values. Maintain clipping to [1, max_los] but avoid rounding a scaled value.
los-empirical-scaling-rounding-causes-di.key_insight: For discrete time-to-exit processes, adjust distribution via probability tilting on the original integer support rather than scaling sampled values and rounding.

blueprint_refs: Train NPE posterior p(θ|x) on simulated pairs; then condition on x_o, sample posterior, and take posterior mean as optimized_parameters.

evidence.metrics: Calibration loss_history decreases to ~0.95 but val_loss remains ~36, indicating good surrogate fit does not translate to better trajectory MSE

posterior-surrogate-calibration-objectiv.error_identification: The calibrator’s neural surrogate training objective (Gaussian NLL on standardized θ) improves substantially, but downstream evaluation MSE does not improve, implying the inferred θ is not well-aligned with minimizing trajectory MSE.
posterior-surrogate-calibration-objectiv.root_cause_analysis: Blueprint expects an SBI posterior; current implementation uses a diagonal Gaussian posterior surrogate and then performs a heuristic candidate search. This can be poorly calibrated for multi-modal or heteroscedastic posteriors and can overemphasize matching θ distribution rather than directly optimizing x reconstruction. Candidate selection uses only train_states[0] flattened MSE, which can still select θ that overfits the single observation and generalizes poorly.
posterior-surrogate-calibration-objectiv.correct_approach: Keep the same structure but align selection more robustly: (1) during candidate selection, score each candidate not only on x_o MSE but also on a small set of auxiliary summaries computed from x (e.g., per-dimension time-averages/variances derived from the same 7-D array) to reduce degenerate fits; implement inside NPEGaussianCalibrator.fit without changing outputs. (2) Increase stochastic averaging for the score: for each candidate θ, run multiple rollouts with different RNG substreams (seeded deterministically from θ hash + base seed) and score the mean MSE; this reduces selecting lucky noise fits and improves validation stability.
posterior-surrogate-calibration-objectiv.key_insight: If posterior learning is approximate, selecting θ should be noise-robust and summary-aware; otherwise the selector overfits a single noisy rollout and won’t improve validation.

main-executes-on-import-causes-integrati.error_identification: The script calls main() at module import time, which can break evaluation harnesses that import the module (e.g., for unit testing or reusing functions) and can cause unexpected side effects.
main-executes-on-import-causes-integrati.root_cause_analysis: At the end of the file, main() is invoked unconditionally instead of being protected by an if __name__ == '__main__' guard.
main-executes-on-import-causes-integrati.correct_approach: Wrap the final main() invocation in a standard __name__ guard so importing the module does not immediately start calibration/evaluation and attempt to read environment variables/files.
main-executes-on-import-causes-integrati.key_insight: Simulation modules should be import-safe; always guard CLI execution to prevent side effects that can masquerade as runtime or evaluation failures.
